statements.attributed: had to increase the MEA grain size to restore strain hardening, dropping yield strength by ~330 MPa to increase uniform elongation to 20%

statements.attributed: reports a monotonic drop in strain hardening rate (Θ) with strain at a stress level ~330 MPa lower

statements.quote: Next, we compare our HGS with two uniformly grained structures in 316L stainless steel (SS) of low SFE .

statements.attributed: reports that lowering yield strength by ~330 MPa only increased uniform elongation to ~10%
statements.quote: Much like the comparison with more-uniform grained MEAs above, here again the SS having a σ0.2 similar to HGS shows a very low Eu (curve 3 in Fig. 2B) and a plunging Θ (Fig. 2C), and lowering σ0.2 by ∼330 MPa only increased Eu to ∼10% (curve 4) , with a monotonic decreasing Θ (Fig. 2C).

statements.attributed: reports that uniform elongation is much lower at any given yield strength compared to HGS
statements.quote: First, comparing our HGS (red solid line) with the more uniform grained MEA (dashed black line), Eu is much increased at any given σ0.2.

statements.attributed: reports that using phase transformation offers high uniform elongation usually at low yield strength (<~400 MPa)
